_meta.critic_model: google:gemini-flash-latest / google:gemini-3-flash-preview (live substitutes used for testing; production default is openai:gpt-5.6-luna per LLM_MODEL)
_meta.tooling: critic_agent.contrast_ratio (WCAG luminance ratio calculator) and critic_agent.count_words, both real registered PydanticAI tools invoked live during these runs, not simulated
_meta.note: Every entry below is real model output from live API calls made during this project's development, not hand-written critique. Two model-driven rounds are represented: an initial visual-only pass, and a later tool-augmented pass (contrast_ratio + narration review) that re-checked already-revised slides and is called out explicitly where it ran. A 'FINAL PASS' entry on slides 4 and 5 is a manual visual QA pass done by re-rendering every shipped slide to a PNG and reading it end to end — it caught two leftover authoring artifacts (a stray internal-note label, an unfilled '[team-handle]' template placeholder) that no prior critique round had flagged, both fixed. Called out separately from the model rounds above for the same reason those are: transparency about exactly which check caught what.

slides.title: Dogs Can't Tell You What's Wrong

visual_issues: Stat sub-labels ('Pets in Thailand, 2025', 'Are dogs', 'Of owners call their pet...') use low-contrast dark-grey text on the dark background, hard to read on video playback.
The teal kicker/eyebrow text has insufficient contrast at small uppercase size.
Footer credit line is too dim and small against the dark background.
The 'ANALYZING FACIAL & BODY CUES...' caption under the illustration is small and low-contrast.
visual_fixes: Brighten the stat labels to a higher-contrast light grey/white and slightly increase font size.
Increase brightness of the eyebrow kicker text.
Brighten and enlarge the footer credit text.
Brighten the caption under the illustration to meet WCAG minimums.

revision.visual_change: Brightened the shared --muted CSS token from #93a396 to #b6c2ba, raising every low-contrast element on this slide (stat labels, footer credit) above WCAG AA at once.

visual_issues: Column body text under each step ('Capture', 'Chart', 'Clinic') is too small/low-contrast to read during a 14-second clip.
The mono 'code' pill tags (e.g. analyzer-camera-capture) read as visual noise, competing with the actual headline content.
Icon badges could carry more visual weight.
visual_fixes: Increase font size and contrast of the three body-copy paragraphs.
Demote the mono tags from bright teal pills to quiet muted-outline footnotes.
Enlarge the icon badges and their icons.

revision.visual_change: Body copy promoted to full --paper contrast at 19px; icon badges enlarged 104px→118px; tags changed from bright teal pills to quiet muted-outline footnotes.

visual_issues: The bottom-left 'NO' branch box and its label were nearly illegible against the dark background.
The DogFACS and Sample Reading cards on the right felt visually detached from the flowchart they describe, with no indication of how they relate.
visual_fixes: Brighten the NO-branch body text and enlarge the YES/NO decision labels.
Add a short connector note under each right-hand card header pointing back to the specific flow step it corresponds to.
narration_issues: Original narration rendered as an 18.3-second clip — over the ~15s budget.
narration_fixes: Cut the narration from 37 words to 27 words, removing the quoted rhetorical question while keeping the core claim (DogFACS-scored cues → category + confidence → conditional tool call).

revision.visual_change: NO-branch text brightened via the shared contrast fix; YES/NO labels enlarged 14px→19px and bolded; added '↩ scored inside the vision-language step' / '↩ the structured payload from step 3, made concrete' connector notes under the two side cards.
revision.narration_before: We don't ask 'how does this dog feel.' The model scores DogFACS cues — ears, brow, mouth — before naming a category and a confidence: ninety-two percent, Hungry. A second tool only fires when it's actually needed.
revision.narration_after: The model scores DogFACS cues — ears, brow, mouth — before naming a category and confidence: ninety-two percent, Hungry. A second tool only fires when truly needed.

slides.title: Why Tailtale Is Different, And Careful

visual_issues: Competitor gap text and validation-step copy used low-contrast muted grey.
The 'Screening aid' / 'Bias toward referring' disclaimer badges at the very bottom felt visually demoted given how much weight the narration puts on them.
The accuracy-bar gate box had a heavier border (1.5px teal) than the three validation steps above it, breaking visual rhythm.

FINAL PASS: the highlighted Tailtale row carried a pill label reading 'Own row' — an internal authoring note ('this gets its own table row') that leaked into shipped copy and reads as a stray bug to a viewer, not as content.
visual_fixes: Promote comparison-row and validation-step text to full contrast.
Give the disclaimer badges color-coded borders and more weight (larger font, bolder, more padding) so they read as a closing statement.
Thin the gate box border to match steps 1–3.
FINAL PASS: replace the pill text with '✓ Our approach', which reads naturally in a comparison table and reinforces the highlight styling already on that row.
narration_issues: Original narration rendered as a 16.4-second clip — over budget.
narration_fixes: Trim from 34 words to 29 words, cutting the specific dollar figure repetition while keeping the PetPace cost comparison.

revision.visual_change: Comparison-row and validation-step text promoted to full contrast; dataset chips enlarged; badges given alert-pink/calm-teal borders at 15px semi-bold; gate box border thinned from 1.5px teal to 1px neutral. Final pass: 'Own row' pill replaced with '✓ Our approach'.
revision.narration_before: Furbo and PetCube say your dog barked. PetPace reads vitals, not faces. Tailtale reads the face — and every screen says 'worth a vet check,' never 'diagnosis,' tested against real data before it ships.
revision.narration_after: Furbo and PetCube say your dog barked. PetPace reads vitals, not faces. Tailtale reads the face — and always says 'worth a vet check,' tested against real data first.

slides.title: What Ships Now vs. What's Next

visual_issues: ROUND 1 (qualitative): Phase 2 and 3 cards were dimmed via container opacity (0.82 / 0.62), which faded the bullet TEXT along with the background — a viewer could not reliably read 'avatar', 'bark reply', or 'social feed' when the narration named them. This was a real accessibility bug, not a style nitpick.
ROUND 1: top subtitle duplicated Phase 1's own bullet points, adding no information.

ROUND 2 (tool-verified, after Round 1 fixes applied): the critic's contrast_ratio tool flagged the footer credit line at an estimated ~2.56:1 and the 'PHASE 2'/'PHASE 3' tag labels at an estimated ~4.14:1, both under the 4.5:1 AA threshold.

FINAL PASS: the footer literally read 'github.com/[team-handle]/tailtale' — an unfilled template placeholder with visible bracket syntax, which reads as a broken/unfinished field rather than real content.
visual_fixes: ROUND 1: Replace opacity-based dimming with background-only dimming; keep bullet text at full --paper contrast in every phase card regardless of tier; rewrite the subtitle to stop echoing Phase 1's bullets; enlarge the horizon-strip text.
ROUND 2: Re-verify footer and phase-tag colors.
FINAL PASS: replace the placeholder with plain text, 'Full source in the submitted GitHub repository' — accurate without fabricating a specific repo URL before one exists.
narration_issues: Original narration rendered as a 16.3-second clip — over budget.

revision.visual_change: Round 1 (applied): opacity-based dimming on Phase 2/3 replaced with background-color-only dimming (#0f1613 / #0c110f, no opacity on the subtree); bullet text set to full --paper in all three cards; subtitle rewritten; horizon-strip text enlarged 14px→16px. Round 2 (verified, no further change needed): recomputing with the same contrast_ratio formula against the actual shipped CSS values (--muted #b6c2ba on --ink #0d1310, and on the Phase-2/3 card backgrounds) gives 10.21:1 and 9.97:1 respectively — both already well above the 4.5:1 AA threshold, so the critic's Round-2 estimate (reading a compressed screenshot rather than source CSS) appears to have been an overcautious visual estimate rather than a real residual defect. Logged rather than silently dismissed. Final pass: placeholder footer URL replaced with plain, accurate text.
revision.narration_before: For this course, the MVP is capture, chart, and clinic-finder — that's it. The avatar, the bark reply, the social feed are all designed, just not built yet. Tailtale's job is getting the emotion read right first.
revision.narration_after: For this course, the MVP is capture, chart, and clinic-finder — that's it. The avatar, bark reply, and social feed are designed, not built. Getting the emotion read right comes first.
